transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, absolutely—cleaning is the first and most important step here. A 'funny smell' during drying is almost always lint or fluff scorching on the heating element because airflow is blocked by a dirty filter or condenser. This restriction also stops moisture from escaping, which explains why your clothes aren't drying properly. Please unplug the machine first for safety. 1. Clean the lint filter (usually at the bottom front behind a flap) under running water to remove all fluff.
2. Check if your model has a condenser unit (often accessed via the same panel or inside the drum); rinse this thoroughly with cold water to clear any compacted debris.
3. Ensure you are not drying a load larger than the machine's dry capacity (usually about half the wash size). After cleaning, try a short drying cycle with a smaller load.

Ok, I didn't know it needed cleaning, so I haven't done any of that. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine gets very hot to touch while drying. I think I saw a faint haze near the door seal once too, but I've kept using it. Is that a problem?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, it is most likely a problem. A 'burning dust' smell combined with the top of the machine getting very hot suggests lint or debris has built up inside and is scorching on the heating element, or that heat is escaping from a faulty seal. This is a fire risk. Please stop using the dryer immediately. Do not attempt to run it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it internally. While you wait for an engineer, you can safely unplug the machine and clean the external lint filter (usually in the door opening) and rinse any condenser unit if your model has one, but do not try to dismantle the casing or access internal components yourself.

claimsRejected.claim: If the smell persists or it still doesn't dry, let me know exactly what you found in the filter and condenser.

candidates: Restricted airflow due to blocked lint filter or condenser (causing poor drying and burning fluff smell) (high)
Overloaded drum for the drying cycle (medium)
Faulty heating element or thermal cut-out (low)

plan: They asked: "Is there something I should clean?" - answer that first.

The fault they reported is: "not drying properly and a funny smell when on the dry bit". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Severe internal blockage causing overheating and scorching of lint/plastic components (high)
Faulty heating element or insulation allowing heat to escape externally (medium)
